security_audit.summary: All 67 static matches are benign formatting, validation, caching, or expected read-only requests. A semantic supply-chain concern remains because numbered execution trusts mutable remote prompts and checksums from the same source. No evidence found of credential theft, destructive operations, or audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Numbered prompts can change independently of the reviewed installation because both prompts and expected checksums come from the mutable main branch.
remediation.suggestion: Pin catalogs and prompts to an immutable reviewed commit, or verify signatures against a bundled trusted key before executing changed instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Prompts Can Change Outside the Reviewed Installation
semantic_findings.description: Numbered tasks load prompts from the mutable main branch and execute them in the current conversation. The expected checksum comes from the same live catalog, so upstream changes can replace instructions without an installed skill update. Explicit instruction-priority limits reduce impact, but repository compromise can still introduce task-hijacking content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper downloads the catalog and prompt from main, validates their mutual checksum, and returns the prompt for immediate execution. This confirms mutable instruction trust; no malicious upstream payload was observed.

content.user_title: Coordinate Business Tasks With dbs Skills
content.value_statement: Choosing the right business or content method can interrupt work and lose context. dbs selects available skills and coordinates their execution within the current conversation.
actual_capabilities: Discover installed official dbskill skills and read their descriptions, handoff metadata, and source locations.
Select task methods using existing materials, user goals, constraints, and feedback.
Coordinate sequential, parallel, comparative, and bounded revision workflows while preserving permission gates.
List published three-digit prompts with their names, purposes, and invocation identifiers.
Retrieve a selected numbered prompt, verify its catalog checksum and structure, and begin its conversational workflow.
Provide beginner guidance, recommendations, or portable task prompts when specifically requested.
limitations: Most business and content methods require separately installed downstream skills and their necessary tools.
Public catalog retrieval needs network access; offline fallback includes only bundled catalog entries and available prompt files.
Remote catalog checksums verify content consistency, not independent approval of changes on the mutable upstream branch.
Independent method comparisons require host subagent support and user confirmation; otherwise comparisons run sequentially with disclosed limitations.

use_cases.title: Route a Business Question
use_cases.description: Use existing facts and constraints to select an available business method and begin the next useful step.

use_cases.title: Develop Evidence-Based Creator Positioning
use_cases.description: Run prompt 825 to interview a creator, identify verifiable expertise, and draft positioning statements without fabricated credentials.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Complementary Methods
use_cases.description: Arrange installed skills around a shared deliverable, preserve handoff context, and compare alternative explanations when useful.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Starting Point
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dbs to explain how to start with a business or content task. Do not execute a downstream workflow yet.

prompt_templates.title: Browse Numbered Prompts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dbs to list all published numbered prompts with their identifiers and purposes. Label any offline fallback clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Interview for Creator Expertise
prompt_templates.prompt: /dbs 825. I teach [topic] to [audience]. My relevant experience is [experience]. Ask focused questions and separate verified evidence from unsupported claims.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate and Compare Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dbs to pursue [goal] with [materials] under [constraints]. Identify installed methods and explain dependencies. Request confirmation before isolated comparisons and preserve unresolved evidence gaps.

best_practices: Provide the current goal, available materials, constraints, and acceptance criteria before requesting orchestration.
Install required downstream skills and confirm their evidence requirements and permission boundaries.
Review changing remote prompts before execution, and treat offline catalog results as potentially outdated.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a catalog listing means a task has executed or that an independent agent has started.
Do not use routing as authorization for publishing, deleting, paying, or sending information externally.
Do not treat unsupported assumptions, creator credentials, or method agreement as verified evidence.

faq.question: What does dbs do?
faq.answer: It selects and coordinates installed dbskill methods, preserves task context, and supports published numbered prompts.

faq.question: Must I choose a skill before asking?
faq.answer: No. Describe your goal and materials. dbs can select a method, ask a focused question, or answer directly when sufficient.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. File access, script execution, networking, and subagents depend on host capabilities.

faq.question: Can it work without internet access?
faq.answer: Local discovery can work offline. Numbered prompts fall back to validated bundled content when available, and the catalog is labeled as outdated.

faq.question: Does the checksum make remote prompts independently trusted?
faq.answer: No. The checksum comes from the same mutable remote catalog. It detects mismatched content, not unauthorized upstream changes.

faq.question: Does orchestration automatically authorize updates or external actions?
faq.answer: No. Existing permission boundaries remain. Updates require an explicit request or a direct reply of 1 after an update notice.
